tools.kind: Content-free source patch (`.py` / `.pyx` / Chowdren runtime `.h`/`.cpp`, including the 2026-09-27 deterministic harness `base/harness.{h,cpp}` and the `MultipleTouch` writer) forward-porting `fnmwolf/Anaconda`'s bundled `mmfparser` + Chowdren to the build-296 mobile CCN: image/font/sound/music banks, object and movement records, the Pillow `frombytes` fix, raw-payload capture for undecoded codes, and the arm64 `size_t`/`uint64_t` overload fix. Since 2026-09-30 it also carries the headless images (`base/image.{h,cpp}`: under `CHOWDREN_NO_DRAW` an image keeps the alpha mask collisions read and frees its pixels at load, `harness_headless_images()`; FNaF 4's Night 8 fell from 1.57 GB to about 260 MB with an equal trace) and the pilot's delta lines (`CHOWDREN_PILOT_DELTA`). The runtime tree on this host also holds `CHOWDREN_IMAGE_OVERRIDE` in `image.cpp`, from `sprite-override.patch` (below; the unmerged commit `3cc85fc` until 2026-09-30); this patch leaves it out, so regenerating it means `regen-patch.py --tree` on a copy of the tree without those hunks.

Chowdren `--config`: `get_missing_image` for placeholder image handle `(0,0)`, and an `init()` hook that synthesizes `game.extensions` entries from the frame items (`Layer` → native writer; `Multiple Touch` / `Android object` / `AndroidPlus` / `iOS Plus Object` → generic `ObjectWriter` stub).
Dumps every event parameter whose code is past `parameterLoaders`, with the ACE it attaches to and its raw bytes. Requires the `Parameter.read` capture patch.
Prints every `OnLoop` condition and its parameter loader — the probe that showed mobile loops are numeric `Short` indices, not name expressions.

The simulator's `Random(N)` draws frame by frame (draws so far, LCG state), in the shape the harness traces: two runs of one night and seed that spend the same draws every frame read the same stream, and the first frame where the counts part is where to look. Refuses a `@sixam/core` resolved outside its own checkout (a worktree without `npm ci` loads the parent's model). MODEL_ONLY.
Explicit diagnostic variant enabling the model's existing sourced flags. It does not change core defaults or establish fidelity.

The origin set plus `sourcedFootstepDraws`, `footstepCamMarkers`, `sourcedBoxCountdown`, `sourcedPuppetMoveOrder`, `sourcedHourTable`, and for Custom Night `sourcedParkedMarker`, `sourcedCustomDialOrder` and `sourcedCam8Cancel`: the options under which the model matches the rebuilt no-input Nights 1-6 and the uniform Custom Nights up to each night's terminal loop. Since the replay splits (2026-09-27, late) it also carries `sourcedPromotedMoves`, `sourcedValue5` (in place of `frameValue5` 1), `sourcedOfficeFootsteps`, `sourcedBlackoutClockEnd`, `sourcedBDrainOrder`, `sourcedRoutePass`, `sourcedOfficeRolls`, `sourcedAnimationCount`, `sourcedGatedEvery`, `sourcedBBMoves`, `sourcedExposureValue5` and `sourcedRouteViewDraws`, under which the Night 1, 5 and 7 winner replays match the rebuild to their last or terminal update. Diagnostic; defaults unchanged.

The rebuild set as it stood before the Nights 6-7 options (`sourcedParkedMarker`, `sourcedCustomDialOrder`, `sourcedCam8Cancel`), byte for byte: the file `rebuild-options-census-20260927` scored (`packages/propose/bin/recompile/rebuild-options-census.ts --options`). Its gate finds the scored bytes by hash among the named file and these snapshots. A snapshot, never edited.

The same sourced flags plus the frame-time hook at 60 fps (`frameMs` 50/3, `frameValue5` 1) and `sourcedEveryOrigin`: every countdown loads on the loop it is first reached. `model-draw-trace.ts` turns the two hook constants into per-frame functions. Diagnostic; defaults unchanged.

Scales harness snaps (1024 x 768) to the phone's 2400 x 1080 MediaProjection frame as Display Mode FULL does, with bilinear filtering as the phone's frames show, and prints per-rectangle distances to a phone frame. Frames stay outside the repository.

Chowdren `--config` for the other build-296 mobile CCNs (FNaF 1, 3, 4): the FNaF 2 config's overrides with extension identity resolved by item name (`Multiple Touch`, `Layer object`, `*.KYSO`, `Ini`...), since each game numbers its extension object types differently.
Container wrapper with GL readiness checking and a process deadline that escalates to kill. Run from the external gamesrc directory.

Content-free runtime patch (Chowdren/base only), applied after `mmfparser-chowdren-mobile.patch`: the GL ES 2.0 renderer. The desktop shader layer (`desktop/glslshader.cpp`) on ES 2.0, the packed GLSL 1.20 shaders rewritten at load time as GLSL ES 1.00 (`base/gles2shader.h`), vertex attributes in place of client arrays, and `copy_rect` from the RGBA8 screen FBO; `-DUSE_GLES2=ON` builds the desktop game on a GLES2 context for host checks. The desktop GL build is unchanged (every change is under `CHOWDREN_USE_GLES2`). `git apply` in the anaconda tree; see `android/README.md`. With it, `android/game-CMakeLists.txt` builds GLES2 by default (`-DCHOWDREN_GLES1=ON` keeps the fixed-function 1.1 target) and `android/build-apk.sh` declares ES 2.0 when `libmain.so` links `libGLESv2.so`.

Check (host, no phone, no game content): compiles and links every `base/shaders` pair through `gles2shader.h` on a headless Mesa GL ES 2.0 context (EGL surfaceless), and renders the Perspective shader's PANORAMA branch over a generated texture against the Android runtime's formula. `gles2-shader-check SHADER_DIR [--dump DIR] > result.json`; exit 0 only if all link and PANORAMA matches. Build line in its header.

Device action (host side, no phone): cross-builds one converted game's `libmain.so` for arm64-v8a with the NDK and `game-CMakeLists.txt`. `--gamesrc DIR --chowdren DIR --sdl-src DIR --sdl-lib DIR --openal-src DIR --openal-lib FILE --work DIR [--jobs N]` (niced, `-j2` by default). It refuses a work directory inside the repository. The build fails unless the static openal-soft is linked (`alcOpenDevice` defined) and its OpenSL ES backend imports `slCreateEngine` from `libOpenSLES.so`.

Device action (host side, no phone): patches a private generated FNaF 2 source copy with the read-only office encounter HUD, `practice-state.jsonl` actor/RNG trace, and `practice-input.jsonl` SDL button-edge trace. `--gamesrc DIR`; generated source and all logs stay outside Git.

Device action (host side, no phone): turns private copies of the Android runtime and SDL's Java classes into a device timing instrument. Every update logs, on CLOCK_MONOTONIC, loop start, pump end, events end and swap end, the exact `dt` and `timer_units`, RNG draws and state and the polled button (`calib-updates.jsonl`, with each frame load's seed). Every touch logs its MotionEvent event time, Java receipt and native SDL queue time (`calib-input.jsonl`), and a 16-cell Gray-code beacon of the update index is drawn along the frame's top 8 px. `--chowdren DIR --sdl DIR`; `debug.rebuild.calib` / `debug.rebuild.calib_beacon` = 0 turn them off. Refuses paths inside the repository.

Report (Python 2.7 + the patched mmfparser): a mobile CCN's sound bank as `CSoundBank.preLoad` reads it (the handle space, then the records; a name only when flags & 0x100). It prints each record's res/raw file by the runtime's rule (`s%04d` by **handle**) and every Sample parameter's handle, as one `recompile-sound-probe-v1` JSON object. `probe-sounds.py <anaconda> <application.ccn> [<res/raw dir>]`. Names, handles and sizes only.

Report: `record` adds or replaces one game's row in a `recompile-game-builds-v1` record. The row holds conversion, host binary, a bounded no-input harness boot (frames visited, exit code, GL errors, sample plays), APK hash and package, and its audio record's evidenceId, all derived from the step outputs. `check` re-derives statuses and the evidenceId and resolves each audio record under `results/`.

Check/report: regenerates `mmfparser-chowdren-mobile.patch` in the committed file order. Each section is `git diff HEAD -- <path>` in the anaconda tree; `--add` appends new paths (`git add -N` when untracked). It then verifies the patch against a pristine `git archive 9b00bb4` (`--pristine`): it applies, and the patched copy equals the tree file for file. `--check-only` verifies the committed patch.

Report/check: `record` writes a game's `recompile-sound-map-v1` table. For each bank record it gives the handle, bank index, name, declared length and rate, and its `res/raw` file by the retail rule (`s%04d` by **handle**) with that file's sha256, duration, rate and channels. It adds the converted asset and its play sites, audition correlations against the handle's file and the bank index's file, and phone-measured anchors. `check` re-derives the file names, the declared-length agreement, asset ids, anchors, summary and evidenceId without any audio. In `npm run test:unit` via `test-audio-records.py`.
Synthetic parser and result-classification regressions; FIXTURE only.
The all-20 Custom Night navigation on the corrected 5 x 2 portrait grid (binary `036076d3` on): portraits 4-9 toggled, then Ready. A dump before Ready reads all ten dials at 20.
The FNaF 4 save for Night 8 (`beat5`-`beat7`, `beat8=0`, `test=1`): the Extras Nightmare button then takes eight taps to arm 20/20/20/20 (`shadow` 2).

tools.kind: Device action (dry unless `--live`, under `device-lock-exec.py`) and report: registers one Companion REGION row across the calibration build's beacon cell centres, decodes the update each MediaProjection frame shows, and joins it with the calibration log on CLOCK_MONOTONIC: image stamp after the producing swap, frames already stale when stamped, the helper's reply age, and the updates the capture never showed. `live --out DIR --seconds N --live`, `grade --in DIR [--record FILE]`. The calibration build must be in front with the system UI hidden, and the helper capturing (`cue_setup`).

Device action (dry unless `--live`, under `device-lock-exec.py`): plays a harness input file (a winner's schedule from `schedule-to-input.ts`, with its title and customize rows) on the calibration build through `/system/bin/hid`, two contacts as the transport encodes them. A shell on the phone releases the customize and office parts on the calibration build's `frame N update 1 done` markers, a tick-F row goes out (F - 1) ticks later, and a press on its pointer's release tick is moved one tick (play mode mirrors pointer 0 from the polled button). A watcher on the phone stops `hid` by its PID the moment the office is left (the first marker of any other frame), because hid runs as `app_process` and a kill by the name `hid` matches nothing. Writes the save first and pulls the session's calibration logs after. `plan --input FILE`, `live --input FILE --save FILE --out DIR --live`.

Check (FIXTURE, no device): two-record reports while contact 1 is involved, reports within 0.5 ms of their tick all night, the same-tick press moved one tick, and the three stream parts. In `npm run test:unit`.

Check (FIXTURE, no device): the plans are fixed by their seed, the stream uses the transport's vocabulary (feature report, ready delay, trap-2 release filler), cut and glued log rows are read safely, and chain verdicts follow the pumps. In `npm run test:unit`.

tools.invocation: packages/propose/bin/recompile/pilot/pilot.ts --game fnaf3\|fnaf4 --run DIR --binary FILE --assets FILE --save FILE --policy NAME [--seed N] [--knobs JSON] [--docker] [--stop-frame N] [--no-trace] [--kill-on-loss] [--prefix PILOT_INPUT --branch UPDATE [--hold N]]
tools.kind: Lockstep controller for a rebuilt night. The harness (`CHOWDREN_PILOT_CONNECT=host:port`, in the patch) sends one JSON line per update over TCP, with the frame, tick, graine and globals, and for each object in `CHOWDREN_PILOT_WATCH` its position, window centre, `FixedValue`, alterables, animation or counter value. It then waits for touches. With `CHOWDREN_PILOT_DELTA=1`, which the pilot sets, a line after the first of each frame visit carries only the objects whose serialisation changed, and the pilot merges it into the last full picture. TCP rather than a FIFO because Docker Desktop's bind mounts do not carry a FIFO out of its VM. The game runs natively by default (`NATIVE_ENV`: SDL offscreen video on surfaceless EGL, OpenAL's null device; forcing `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE` crashes EGL), and in the container with `--docker`; the two give the same trace. `--stop-frame 5` ends the run 30 updates into the win frame, `--kill-on-loss` as soon as the policy reports a loss. `--prefix` replays an earlier run's `pilot.input` up to update `--branch` of the play frame, holds `--hold` updates with no touch, and only then lets the policy act (`search.mjs`). Every applied touch is written to `DIR/pilot.input` as a plain `CHOWDREN_INPUT` row, and the summary names the last update seen in the play frame. Host-only; DIR stays outside the repository.

tools.kind: One policy over a block of seeds, natively, stopped at the win frame or killed on a loss. A seed is WON only if the save holds every `--win-key`; a seed whose controller never logged a record never reached the night and is NO_NIGHT, not a loss. One row per seed in `DIR/results.jsonl` (verdict, outcome, updates, the input's sha256, the policy sources' sha256, the last controller records of a loss); an interrupted block resumes, and the batch stops if `pilot.ts` or the game module changes before the block is done. Run it under a memory-capped scope (`systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=...`). Host-only; DIR outside the repository.

tools.invocation: packages/propose/bin/recompile/pilot/search.ts --game G --policy NAME --binary FILE --assets FILE --save FILE --seeds A-B --out DIR --win-key K=V [--budget 24]
tools.kind: Per-seed input search: does some sequence of in-window touches win this seed? After a loss it replays the lost attempt's own touches to a branch point, holds 1-21 updates, and hands back to the policy. The branch points are the updates at which the policy started a task (every one, when the policy reports them in its summary as `guard2` does; else those in its log) merged with 5-80 s steps back, latest first; a hold there delays the task, so every touch that draws from the shared generator draws at a different update. A game module's `doomStart` names where a lost chain began (FNaF 3: an attack stage, a GOT YOU marker, vent 14 or 15), and no branch is taken inside it; a branch whose chain begins more than 2 s later becomes the base, and when a base's points are used up the search backs up to the one before. A WON seed keeps its touches as `win.input`, a plain `CHOWDREN_INPUT`, and the search replays them with no pilot (`replayWon`), after dropping the touch the harness logs across a frame change with the old frame and update 0 (`withoutStrays`). Every row carries the sha256 of `pilot.ts`, the game module, `search.mjs` and `replay.ts`, and the search stops if one changes. It asks whether the night is winnable by touches, not what a player can do.

`recompile-pilot-night-v1`: hashes of the binary, assets, save and input, the two trace digests, the frames visited, and the save keys the game wrote. It is WON only if the replay's trace equals the pilot's and every `--win-key` is absent before the night and written by it. `check` re-derives the verdict and evidenceId.

Re-derives every committed pilot record and refuses a fixture touch outside the 1024 x 768 window. Its negative controls must fail: a diverged replay, a win key already in the save, a missing win key, a changed seed. It pins `SEAL_FOR`/`LURE_TO` to the core FNaF 3 graph and lure table (`sim-fnaf3.js`), the play budget (`playsLeft`) and the 66 rare-screen seeds (`whatDayRare`). In `npm run test:unit`; no binary.

tools.invocation: packages/review/bin/recompile/phone-audio-cues.py CAPTURE.wav --refs DIR --cues LIST [--anchor NAME=T,... ...] [--anchor-plays PLAYS.json --anchor-cues LIST] [--json OUT]
tools.kind: Matched-filter onsets of extracted game samples in a phone's A2DP capture (0.4 s cores, NCC, near-silent stretches excluded), aligned to the game clock by a solved offset: every (anchor onset, known play) pair proposes one, the offset most anchor onsets agree with (within 0.1 s) wins, and it is refused as AMBIGUOUS (exit 3, no game times) unless it leads every offset more than 0.2 s away by three onsets. Anchor plays come from `NAME=T,...` or a `rebuild-audio-plays-v1` record. A periodic anchor alone (the mask sound every window) fits every whole period: the 2026-09-28 full-06 read, which paired each onset with the nearest play within 1 s, was 30 s late. A match is a sound in the mix, not the event that played it; a miss is UNKNOWN. Needs numpy and scipy (`solve_offset` does not); DEVICE_MEASURED audio, arithmetic alignment.
